chunks: Among them is what Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Walid al-Khazzaz from Yunus ibn Yaqub, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
Allah did not accept to appoint to it (the Imamate) two brothers after Hasan and Husain (peace be upon them).
ai.seo_question: Who were the two brothers after whom the Imamate was not appointed according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to highlight the unique divine decree regarding the Imamate of Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s), who had no sons, thereby distinguishing his era from the general pattern of hereditary succession. This specific exclusion of 'two brothers' underscores the miraculous nature of the subsequent emergence of Imam al-Mahdi (a.j) as the sole heir, reinforcing the concept of *al-Imamah* being a divine appointment rather than merely a familial right. It serves as a key argument in Shia theology for the validity of the Hidden Imam's lineage and authority.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 190 - Narrated Saad bin Abdullah from Muhammad bin Walid Khazzaz from Yunus bin Yaqub from Abi Abdullah (a.s) that he said: “
Allah does not accept to appoint to it (the Imamate) two brothers after Hasan and Husain (a.s).”
